title: Domain of the Composite sqrt(1/(x - 1))
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Given f(x) = sqrt(x) and g(x) = 1/(x - 1), find the domain of the composite f o g and explain how the constraints from both the inner and outer functions combine.

steps.title: Write the Composite Explicitly
steps.explanation: Applying g first and feeding its output into f produces the single radical expression whose domain is sought.
steps.why: Domain questions for compositions are best answered on the explicit formula, tracking every restriction at once.

steps.title: Collect the Inner Restriction
steps.explanation: The reciprocal g has a denominator that cannot vanish, so x = 1 is excluded before the outer function is even consulted.
steps.why: Composition requires the inner function to produce a value at all; an undefined inner output makes the whole composite undefined.

steps.title: Collect the Outer Restriction
steps.explanation: The square root accepts only nonnegative inputs, so the sign of the fraction must be checked: its numerator is the positive constant 1.
steps.why: A fraction with a strictly positive numerator is nonnegative exactly when its denominator is positive, i.e. x - 1 > 0.

steps.title: Intersect the Constraints
steps.explanation: The sign condition x > 1 already rules out x = 1 and is stricter than x != 1, so the intersection is simply the open ray (1, infinity).
steps.why: The domain of a composite is where every stage is legal simultaneously; here the outer radical condition dominates the inner one.
